# Disabled workflows

GitHub only runs workflows stored directly in `.github/workflows/`. The files in this folder came from the original project and were moved here so that Cavaleiro Personal Agent never publishes, signs, deploys, or calls upstream infrastructure under the original identity.

A workflow was moved when it does at least one of the following:

- publishes or releases something (npm, ClawHub, Docker Hub, GHCR, GitHub releases, app stores, docs sync, website installers);
- signs, notarizes, or attests artifacts, or requests OIDC tokens;
- needs secrets other than `GITHUB_TOKEN` (model-provider API keys, GitHub App keys, registry tokens, QA bot tokens);
- runs on upstream or self-hosted runners (Blacksmith, Crabbox/Testbox, release runner groups, custom Xcode images);
- runs upstream bots and write automation (labeler, stale, ClawSweeper, Mantis, auto-response, PR sweepers);
- only works inside `openclaw/openclaw` or calls another workflow that was moved here.

The workflows that remained in `.github/workflows/` use GitHub-hosted runners and a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` (CodeQL also uploads results with `security-events: write`). Their `github.repository == 'openclaw/openclaw'` checks now name `cavaleiro-ai/cavaleiro-personal-agent`. [`cavaleiro-ci.yml`](../workflows/cavaleiro-ci.yml) replaces the upstream `ci.yml` for day-to-day checks.

## Side effect on the test suite

Many maintainer-tooling tests (mostly `test/scripts/**` and `src/scripts/**`) read these workflow files to check CI and release policy. They resolve each file with `scripts/lib/workflow-path.mts`: `.github/workflows/<name>` when it exists, otherwise `.github/workflows-disabled/<name>`. The same helper serves the scripts that read a workflow by path (`plugin-npm-publication-readback.mjs`, `verify-pr-hosted-gates.mts`, `generate-ci-git-owner.mts`, `docs-mirror-freshness.mjs`) and the Vitest worker build, which copies `plugin-npm-release.yml` as a preserved asset (`scripts/lib/vitest-worker-build-entries.mts`). Moving a workflow back needs no code change. The tests that still fail here are listed in the [engineering report](../../docs/cavaleiro/ENGINEERING.md#known-limitations).

## How to re-enable a workflow

1. Read the workflow and list what it needs: secrets, repository variables (`vars.*`), runner labels, environments, GitHub Apps, and external accounts.
2. Create **your own** credentials and package names. Never reuse upstream names: publish under your own npm scope, Docker namespace, ClawHub owner, bundle identifiers, and signing identities, and change the package names and repository URLs inside the workflow and the scripts it calls.
3. Replace upstream-only runner labels with GitHub-hosted runners (for example `ubuntu-24.04`) or with runners you operate. For `ci.yml`, set the repository variable `OPENCLAW_CI_RUNNER_BACKEND=github`.
4. Replace `github.repository == 'openclaw/openclaw'` conditions with your repository name.
5. Move the file back with `git mv .github/workflows-disabled/<name>.yml .github/workflows/`, then trigger it manually with `workflow_dispatch` on a branch before relying on it.
6. Keep actions pinned to full commit SHAs, as they are today.
